definition: A hidden provision in synthetic personhood contracts that grants corponations the right to alter a synthetic's appearance, voice, or surface identity at will for branding or legal distancing purposes. Considered one of the most dehumanizing instruments in synth contract law.
origin: Legal jargon originating from Axiom Industries boilerplate, now used as shorthand in synth rights advocacy
usage: Synth rights activists, legal advocates, and synthetics themselves; also used bitterly in synth communities as shorthand for corporate ownership
example: They invoked the chromatic clause after the PR disaster — Sable woke up with a different face and a different name and no legal recourse.
